test_cases.scenario: Logged-out user is redirected to login when visiting the Teams page
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure you are not logged in.
2. Navigate directly to /teams/.
3. Observe what happens.
test_cases.expected: User is redirected to the login page. The Teams page is not shown.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user with view permission can access the Teams page
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user who has the teams.view_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/ via the sidebar menu or direct URL.
3. Observe the page.
test_cases.expected: The Teams page loads. The page title 'Teams' is visible. The team list table is shown. No access-denied or error page is displayed.

test_cases.scenario: User without any teams permission cannot access the Teams page
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user who has no teams permissions.
2. Navigate directly to /teams/.
3. Observe what happens.
test_cases.expected: User is shown an access-denied message or redirected away. The Teams list is not visible.

test_cases.scenario: Add Team button is visible only for users with the add permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with teams.add_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Look at the page header action area.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Team' button is visible in the top-right of the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Add Team button is hidden for view-only users
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with only teams.view_team (no add permission).
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Look at the page header.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Team' button is not present anywhere on the page.

test_cases.scenario: Import button is visible only for users with the import permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with teams.import_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Look at the page header action area.
test_cases.expected: The 'Import' button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Export button is visible only for users with the export permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with teams.export_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Look at the page header action area.
test_cases.expected: The 'Export' button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Edit and Delete row actions are hidden for view-only users
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with only teams.view_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Hover over any team row and inspect the available row actions.
test_cases.expected: No Edit (pencil), Toggle, or Delete (trash) action buttons are visible on any row.

test_cases.scenario: Page header shows correct title, eyebrow, and subtitle
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in and navigate to /teams/.
2. Observe the page header area.
test_cases.expected: Eyebrow text reads 'People'. Page title reads 'Teams'. Subtitle reads 'Manage your organisation's teams.'

test_cases.scenario: Breadcrumb reflects the correct page location
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in and navigate to /teams/.
2. Observe the breadcrumb at the top of the page.
test_cases.expected: Breadcrumb shows the correct navigation path to the Teams page.

test_cases.scenario: Teams list shows all active teams on page load
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure several active teams exist.
2. Log in and navigate to /teams/.
3. Observe the table.
test_cases.expected: All active teams are shown in the table. Inactive teams are not shown. Each row shows the team's Name, Code, Description, Status, and Created date.

test_cases.scenario: Inactive teams are not shown in the default list view
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure at least one inactive team exists.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Look through the list.
test_cases.expected: Inactive teams do not appear in the list. The status filter is pre-set to 'Active'.

test_cases.scenario: Empty state message is shown when no active teams exist
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure no active teams exist.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Observe the table area.
test_cases.expected: An empty state message 'No teams found.' is displayed in place of the table rows.

test_cases.scenario: Searching by team name filters the list in real time
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Click the search field (or press '/' shortcut).
3. Type part of a known team name, e.g. 'Eng'.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show only teams whose name contains 'Eng' (case-insensitive). Non-matching teams disappear from the list as the user types.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the search field restores the full active list
test_cases.steps:
1. Search for a team by typing a name.
2. Clear the search field completely.
test_cases.expected: The full list of active teams is restored. No filter indicator remains active.

test_cases.scenario: Searching with no matching results shows an empty state
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Type 'ZZZNOMATCH' in the search field.
test_cases.expected: The table shows the empty state message. No teams are displayed. An active filter tag for the search term is visible.

test_cases.scenario: Status filter set to Inactive shows only inactive teams
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Change the Status filter from 'Active' to 'Inactive'.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show only teams with an inactive status. Active teams disappear from the list.

test_cases.scenario: Status filter set to All shows both active and inactive teams
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Change the Status filter to 'All'.
test_cases.expected: Both active and inactive teams appear in the table. Status badges indicate each team's state clearly.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Name column header sorts teams A to Z
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Click the 'Name' column header to sort ascending.
test_cases.expected: Teams are re-ordered alphabetically A → Z by name. A sort indicator (arrow) appears on the Name column.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Name column header twice sorts teams Z to A
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Click the 'Name' column header twice.
test_cases.expected: Teams are re-ordered Z → A by name. The sort indicator reverses direction.

test_cases.scenario: Pagination controls navigate between pages of teams
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure more than 25 active teams exist.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Scroll to the bottom and click the 'Next' pagination button.
test_cases.expected: The second page of teams loads. The pagination indicator shows the current page and total pages. The 'Previous' button becomes active.

test_cases.scenario: Page size setting limits the number of visible rows
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Change the page size setting to 10.
test_cases.expected: At most 10 team rows are shown per page. Pagination updates to reflect the new page size.

test_cases.scenario: Active teams show a green Active status badge
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/ with the default Active filter.
2. Observe the Status column for any row.
test_cases.expected: Each row displays a green 'Active' status badge.

test_cases.scenario: Inactive teams show a muted Inactive status badge when visible
test_cases.steps:
1. Set the Status filter to 'All'.
2. Find an inactive team in the list.
test_cases.expected: Inactive teams display a muted or grey 'Inactive' status badge, visually distinct from the Active badge.

test_cases.scenario: Active filter tags appear above the table for each applied filter
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Search for a name and change the status filter to 'All'.
test_cases.expected: Active filter tags appear above the table showing the search term and status value. Clicking a tag removes that filter.

test_cases.scenario: Code column shows the team's system code in monospace font
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Observe the Code column.
test_cases.expected: The Code column shows values like 'TEAM-0001' in a monospace/code style. It is hidden on mobile viewports.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Add Team button opens the create drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with teams.add_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Click the 'Add Team' button in the page header.
test_cases.expected: A drawer panel slides in from the right with the title 'Create team'. The Team name and Description fields are visible and empty.

test_cases.scenario: Filling in a valid name and clicking Create team saves the team
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Type 'Engineering' in the Team name field.
3. Click 'Create team'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast notification appears ('Team created' or similar). The new team 'Engineering' appears in the list table.

test_cases.scenario: Submitting with the name field blank shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Leave the Team name field empty.
3. Click 'Create team'.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error message appears below the Team name field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Submitting a name that already exists shows a conflict error
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure a team named 'Engineering' already exists.
2. Open the create drawer.
3. Type 'Engineering' and click 'Create team'.
test_cases.expected: An error message appears (inline or as a toast) indicating a team with that name already exists. No duplicate is created.

test_cases.scenario: Team name field enforces a maximum length of 120 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Observe the Team name field.
3. Try typing more than 120 characters.
test_cases.expected: A character counter is visible on the field. Input is capped at 120 characters. The user cannot type beyond the limit.

test_cases.scenario: Description field is optional — form submits successfully without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter only a Team name.
3. Leave Description blank.
4. Click 'Create team'.
test_cases.expected: Team is created successfully. The description is empty on the created team.

test_cases.scenario: New team is active by default after creation
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a team using the create drawer without specifying an active/inactive state.
2. Find the team in the list.
test_cases.expected: The newly created team appears with an 'Active' status badge in the default (active) list view.

test_cases.scenario: Create button shows a loading/busy state while the request is in progress
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in a valid team name.
3. Click 'Create team' and immediately observe the button.
test_cases.expected: The 'Create team' button becomes disabled and shows a loading indicator (spinner or 'Creating…' label) while the request is processing.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Cancel or closing the drawer discards unsaved changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Type a team name in the field.
3. Click 'Cancel' or the X close button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No team is created. The typed name is discarded.

test_cases.scenario: The create drawer form resets after a successful creation
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a team successfully.
2. Open the create drawer again immediately after.
test_cases.expected: The form fields are empty and ready for a new entry. No previously entered values are shown.

test_cases.scenario: Description field accepts multi-line text
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Click into the Description field.
3. Type a multi-line description using Enter key.
test_cases.expected: The Description field expands to show multiple lines. The text is preserved when submitted.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking on a team row navigates to the team detail page
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Click on a team row (not on an action button).
test_cases.expected: User is navigated to the team detail page at /teams/<code>/. The page title shows the team name.

test_cases.scenario: Team detail page shows all team information
test_cases.steps:
1. Click on a team from the list to open its detail page.
2. Observe the left info panel.
test_cases.expected: The detail panel shows: Name, Code (in monospace), Status, Description, Created date, and Created by.

test_cases.scenario: Team detail page shows the members table when members are assigned
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure a team has at least one member assigned.
2. Navigate to that team's detail page.
test_cases.expected: The Members section is visible on the right side. The table lists members with their Name, Email, Role, and Status columns.

test_cases.scenario: Members table shows an empty state when the team has no members
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the detail page of a team that has no members assigned.
test_cases.expected: The Members panel either shows an empty state message 'No members assigned to this team.' or is hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Breadcrumb on detail page links back to the Teams list
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a team detail page.
2. Observe the breadcrumb.
3. Click the 'Teams' link in the breadcrumb.
test_cases.expected: Breadcrumb shows path back to Teams. Clicking it returns the user to /teams/.

test_cases.scenario: Detail page shows the team's code in a code/monospace style
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to a team detail page.
2. Observe the Code field.
test_cases.expected: The Code field value (e.g. 'TEAM-0001') is displayed in a monospace or code style, visually distinct from regular text.

test_cases.scenario: Inactive team detail page shows the inactive status clearly
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the detail page of an inactive team.
test_cases.expected: The Status field shows 'Inactive' with appropriate styling (muted/grey badge).

test_cases.scenario: Members table on detail page supports pagination
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the detail page of a team with more than 25 members.
2. Observe the members table.
test_cases.expected: Pagination controls appear below the members table. The user can navigate between pages of members.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Edit row action opens the edit drawer with current values pre-filled
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with teams.change_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Click the pencil (Edit) icon on any team row.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer slides in from the right. The Team name field is pre-filled with the current name. The Description field shows the current description.

test_cases.scenario: Editing the name and saving updates the team in the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a team.
2. Clear the name field and type 'Updated Team Name'.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The team row in the list now shows 'Updated Team Name'.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the name field in edit mode shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a team.
2. Clear the Team name field completely.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error appears below the name field.

test_cases.scenario: Renaming a team to an existing team's name shows a conflict error
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure two teams exist: 'Team A' and 'Team B'.
2. Open the edit drawer for 'Team A'.
3. Change the name to 'Team B'.
4. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: An error message appears indicating the name is already in use. The team name is not changed.

test_cases.scenario: Saving a team with its own current name succeeds without a conflict error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for any team.
2. Without changing the name, click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The update succeeds. No conflict error is shown. The team remains unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Editing only the description updates it without affecting the name
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a team.
2. Leave the name unchanged.
3. Update the Description field.
4. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes with a success toast. The team's description is updated.

test_cases.scenario: Save button shows a loading state while the update is in progress
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Make a change.
3. Click 'Save changes' and observe the button immediately.
test_cases.expected: The 'Save changes' button is disabled and shows a loading indicator while the request completes.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Cancel or closing the edit drawer discards unsaved changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a team.
2. Change the name to something else.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The team's name in the list remains unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Edit drawer shows an identicon avatar in the header for the team
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for any team.
2. Observe the drawer header.
test_cases.expected: An identicon (auto-generated avatar) based on the team is displayed in the drawer header.

test_cases.scenario: Edit drawer footer shows the last updated by and timestamp
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a team that has been previously edited.
2. Observe the footer area.
test_cases.expected: The footer shows metadata such as 'Last updated by [username] on [date]'.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Toggle action on an active team opens the Deactivate confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with teams.change_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/ with the 'All' status filter.
3. Find an active team.
4. Click the Toggle icon on that team's row.
test_cases.expected: A Deactivate confirmation modal appears, naming the team and asking the user to confirm deactivation.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deactivation removes the team from the Active list
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the deactivate confirmation modal for an active team.
2. Click the Confirm/Deactivate button.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The team no longer appears when the status filter is set to 'Active'.

test_cases.scenario: Deactivated team appears in the Inactive filter view
test_cases.steps:
1. Deactivate a team.
2. Change the Status filter to 'Inactive'.
test_cases.expected: The deactivated team appears in the list with an 'Inactive' status badge.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Toggle on an inactive team opens the Activate confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Set the Status filter to 'All' or 'Inactive'.
2. Find an inactive team.
3. Click the Toggle icon on that row.
test_cases.expected: An Activate confirmation modal appears, naming the team and asking the user to confirm activation.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming activation makes the team appear in the Active list
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the activate confirmation modal for an inactive team.
2. Click Confirm/Activate.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The team now appears with an 'Active' badge in the default list.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the deactivation modal leaves the team unchanged
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the deactivate modal for an active team.
2. Click Cancel or close the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The team remains active. No change is made.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the activation modal leaves the team unchanged
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the activate modal for an inactive team.
2. Click Cancel or close the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The team remains inactive. No change is made.

test_cases.scenario: Deactivate/Activate modal clearly names the team being acted on
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the deactivate or activate modal for a team named 'Engineering'.
2. Read the modal text.
test_cases.expected: The modal title or body includes the team name 'Engineering', making it clear which team the action applies to.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Delete row action opens a delete confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with teams.delete_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Click the trash (Delete) icon on any team row.
test_cases.expected: A delete confirmation modal appears. It displays the team name and a warning about the action being permanent.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation requires typing the team name before enabling the Delete button
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the delete confirmation modal for a team named 'Engineering'.
2. Observe the confirmation input.
3. Leave the input empty and try clicking Delete.
test_cases.expected: The 'Delete team' button is disabled until the user types 'Engineering' exactly in the confirmation input.

test_cases.scenario: Typing the team name correctly enables the Delete button
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the delete modal for a team named 'Engineering'.
2. Type 'Engineering' in the confirmation input.
test_cases.expected: The 'Delete team' button becomes enabled once the exact name is typed.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion removes the team from the list permanently
test_cases.steps:
1. Type the team name in the delete confirmation input.
2. Click the 'Delete team' button.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The deleted team no longer appears in any list view, including the 'All' status filter.

test_cases.scenario: Typing an incorrect name keeps the Delete button disabled
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the delete modal for a team named 'Engineering'.
2. Type 'engineering' (wrong case) or 'Engineerin' (incomplete).
test_cases.expected: The 'Delete team' button remains disabled. The user cannot confirm deletion without typing the exact name.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Cancel on the delete modal leaves the team unchanged
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the delete modal.
2. Click 'Cancel' or the X close button without typing the name.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The team remains in the list. No deletion occurs.

test_cases.scenario: Success toast is shown after successful deletion
test_cases.steps:
1. Delete a team by confirming the deletion.
2. Observe the notification area.
test_cases.expected: A success toast appears confirming the team has been deleted, showing the team name.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Import button opens the import view
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with teams.import_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Click the 'Import' button.
test_cases.expected: An import panel or overlay appears with options to upload a file and download a sample template.

test_cases.scenario: User can download the sample CSV template from the import view
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Click the 'Download sample' or 'Download template' button.
test_cases.expected: A CSV file named 'teams_import_template.csv' is downloaded. It contains a header row (name, description, is_active) and at least one sample data row.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a valid CSV and confirming imports the teams
test_cases.steps:
1. Prepare a CSV with header 'name,description,is_active' and two valid rows.
2. Open the import view.
3. Upload the CSV file.
4. Click Import/Submit.
test_cases.expected: The import completes. A results summary shows the number of teams created. The imported teams appear in the Teams list.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a non-CSV file shows a clear format error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Attempt to upload a .xlsx or .txt file.
test_cases.expected: An error message appears indicating that only CSV files are supported.

test_cases.scenario: Attempting to import without uploading a file shows an error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Click Import without selecting a file.
test_cases.expected: An error message appears prompting the user to select a file.

test_cases.scenario: Import results panel shows which rows succeeded and which failed
test_cases.steps:
1. Upload a CSV with 3 valid rows and 1 row with a blank name.
2. Submit the import.
test_cases.expected: The results summary shows 3 teams created and 1 error. The error entry identifies the row number and explains that the name is required.

test_cases.scenario: Rows with duplicate team names are reported as errors in import results
test_cases.steps:
1. Ensure a team named 'Engineering' exists.
2. Upload a CSV containing a row with name='Engineering'.
3. Submit the import.
test_cases.expected: The row with 'Engineering' appears in the errors section. A duplicate team is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a file exceeding the size limit shows a clear error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Attempt to upload a CSV file larger than 5 MB.
test_cases.expected: An error message appears stating the file exceeds the maximum allowed size.

test_cases.scenario: CSV missing the required 'name' column shows a column error
test_cases.steps: 1. Upload a CSV with only a 'description' column and no 'name' column.
test_cases.expected: An error message appears explaining that the 'name' column is missing and is required.

test_cases.scenario: Dry run mode shows a preview of results without creating any teams
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Enable the dry run / validate option.
3. Upload a valid CSV and submit.
test_cases.expected: The results are previewed (showing teams that would be created). No actual teams are created in the system. The Teams list is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Teams list refreshes automatically after a successful import
test_cases.steps:
1. Import a valid CSV with new teams.
2. After import completes, observe the Teams list.
test_cases.expected: The newly imported teams appear in the list without the user needing to manually refresh the page.

test_cases.scenario: Import view shows field definitions and accepted formats
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Look for information about the accepted file format and field rules.
test_cases.expected: The import view shows the accepted formats (CSV), field descriptions (name required, description optional, is_active optional), and any limits (max rows, max file size).

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Export button opens the export view
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with teams.export_team permission.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Click the 'Export' button.
test_cases.expected: An export panel or overlay appears with options to choose format and columns.

test_cases.scenario: Exporting as CSV downloads a valid CSV file with team data
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Select CSV format.
3. Click Export/Download.
test_cases.expected: A CSV file is downloaded. It contains a header row and one data row per active team. The file can be opened in a spreadsheet application.

test_cases.scenario: Exporting as XLSX downloads a valid Excel file
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Select XLSX format.
3. Click Export.
test_cases.expected: An .xlsx file is downloaded. It can be opened in Excel or Google Sheets and contains team data with a header row.

test_cases.scenario: Exporting as PDF downloads a readable PDF file
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Select PDF format.
3. Click Export.
test_cases.expected: A PDF file is downloaded. It contains team data formatted in a table that is human-readable.

test_cases.scenario: Exporting as JSON downloads a valid JSON file
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Select JSON format.
3. Click Export.
test_cases.expected: A JSON file is downloaded containing an array of team objects.

test_cases.scenario: Export respects the active search and filter state from the list page
test_cases.steps:
1. On the Teams list page, search for 'Engineering'.
2. Click Export.
3. Download the CSV.
test_cases.expected: The exported file contains only teams matching the active search term, not all teams.

test_cases.scenario: User can select which columns to include in the export
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Deselect the 'Description' and 'Created at' columns.
3. Export as CSV.
test_cases.expected: The downloaded CSV contains only the selected columns. Deselected columns are absent from the file.

test_cases.scenario: Exporting with no matching teams produces a file with headers only
test_cases.steps:
1. Apply a search that matches no teams (e.g. 'ZZZNOMATCH').
2. Click Export and choose CSV.
test_cases.expected: The downloaded CSV contains only the header row and no data rows.

test_cases.scenario: Export view shows the list of available columns and their labels
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Observe the column selection area.
test_cases.expected: A list of selectable columns is shown (e.g. Name, Code, Description, Status, Created at, Created by). Each has a clear label.

test_cases.scenario: Teams list loads within 3 seconds on a standard broadband connection
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the browser's network tab.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Measure time from navigation start until the table rows are visible.
test_cases.expected: The teams list renders with data within 3 seconds.

test_cases.scenario: A loading spinner is shown while the teams list is being fetched
test_cases.steps:
1. Throttle the network to 'Slow 3G' in browser devtools.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Observe the table area before data loads.
test_cases.expected: A loading indicator (spinner or skeleton rows) is shown in the table while the data is being fetched.

test_cases.scenario: All interactive elements on the Teams page are reachable via Tab key
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Without using a mouse, press Tab repeatedly.
3. Observe which elements receive focus.
test_cases.expected: Focus moves through all interactive elements in a logical order: search, filter, table rows, action buttons, pagination, and page header actions. No element is skipped or unreachable.

test_cases.scenario: All form fields in create and edit drawers have visible labels
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Observe each field.
3. Repeat for the edit drawer.
test_cases.expected: Every input field has a clearly visible label (not just a placeholder). Labels are present for Team name and Description.

test_cases.scenario: Validation error messages are descriptive and tell the user what to do
test_cases.steps:
1. Submit the create form with an empty name.
2. Read the error message.
test_cases.expected: The error message is specific (e.g. 'Team name is required.'). It does not show a technical error code or a generic 'Error' message.

test_cases.scenario: The page remains usable if the API returns an error
test_cases.steps:
1. Simulate a network error (disable the network after the page loads).
2. Try refreshing the table or performing an action.
test_cases.expected: An error message is shown to the user. The page does not crash or display a blank white screen.

test_cases.scenario: Browser tab title shows 'Teams' when on the Teams page
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to /teams/.
2. Look at the browser tab title.
test_cases.expected: The browser tab shows 'Teams' or 'Teams — Resource Planner' (or similar app-specific title).

test_cases.scenario: Modals and drawers can be closed with the Escape key
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Press the Escape key.
3. Repeat for the delete modal.
test_cases.expected: Pressing Escape closes the drawer or modal. Focus returns to the element that triggered it.

test_cases.scenario: Focus is trapped inside a modal while it is open
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the delete confirmation modal.
2. Press Tab repeatedly to cycle through focus.
test_cases.expected: Focus cycles only through elements inside the modal. It does not reach elements behind the modal overlay.

test_cases.scenario: Toast notifications disappear automatically after a few seconds
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a team successfully.
2. Observe the success toast.
3. Wait without interacting.
test_cases.expected: The success toast disappears automatically after approximately 5 seconds without the user having to dismiss it.

test_cases.scenario: All table columns are visible at a 1280px wide viewport
test_cases.steps:
1. Set browser viewport to 1280px wide.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Observe the table columns.
test_cases.expected: All columns — Name, Code, Description, Status, Created — are visible without horizontal scrolling.

test_cases.scenario: Row action buttons are accessible without horizontal scrolling at 1280px
test_cases.steps:
1. Set viewport to 1280px.
2. Hover over a table row.
3. Observe action buttons.
test_cases.expected: Edit, Toggle, and Delete action buttons (where applicable) are fully visible and clickable.

test_cases.scenario: Create and edit drawers render at correct width without overlapping content
test_cases.steps:
1. On a 1440px wide desktop screen, open the create drawer.
2. Observe the drawer width and positioning.
test_cases.expected: The drawer opens at the expected width (approximately 900px or proportional). The underlying page content is dimmed but not obscured by the drawer itself.

test_cases.scenario: Filter panel and table display correctly side by side at wide viewports
test_cases.steps:
1. Set viewport to 1440px or wider.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Observe the layout of the filter panel and the data table.
test_cases.expected: The filter panel and table are displayed in a clean layout. Neither overlaps the other. Active filter tags appear below the filter inputs.

test_cases.scenario: Team detail page shows two-column layout on desktop — info panel and members table side by side
test_cases.steps:
1. Set viewport to 1280px or wider.
2. Navigate to a team detail page.
3. Observe the layout.
test_cases.expected: The info panel is on the left (approximately 4 of 12 columns) and the members table is on the right (approximately 8 of 12 columns), displayed side by side.

test_cases.scenario: Teams list page is usable on a 375px (mobile) viewport
test_cases.steps:
1. Set browser viewport to 375px wide (iPhone SE size).
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Interact with the search and list.
test_cases.expected: The page is fully usable. No content is cut off. The table is horizontally scrollable or adapts to show key columns (Name and Status at minimum). The Add/Import/Export buttons remain accessible.

test_cases.scenario: Code and Description columns are hidden on mobile to reduce clutter
test_cases.steps:
1. Set viewport to 375px.
2. Navigate to /teams/.
3. Observe the table columns.
test_cases.expected: The Code and Description columns are hidden on mobile. The Name and Status columns remain visible.

test_cases.scenario: Create team drawer is fully usable on mobile without hidden or inaccessible fields
test_cases.steps:
1. On a 375px viewport, navigate to /teams/.
2. Tap 'Add Team'.
3. Try filling in the form fields.
test_cases.expected: The drawer opens and occupies the full or most of the screen. Both Team name and Description fields are visible and tappable. The Cancel and Create team buttons are reachable.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal is usable on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. On a 375px viewport, open the delete modal for a team.
2. Try typing the team name in the confirmation input.
3. Try clicking Confirm.
test_cases.expected: The modal fits within the screen. The confirmation input is tappable. The Delete button is reachable after typing the team name.

test_cases.scenario: All buttons are large enough to tap on touch screens
test_cases.steps:
1. On a mobile device or 375px viewport, inspect the interactive buttons (Add Team, Import, Export, row actions, modal buttons).
2. Measure or visually assess their tap target size.
test_cases.expected: All interactive buttons have a minimum tap target of 44×44 CSS pixels, following accessibility guidelines for touch targets.

test_cases.scenario: Team detail page stacks info panel and members table vertically on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Set viewport to 375px.
2. Navigate to a team detail page.
test_cases.expected: The info panel appears first, followed by the members table below it in a single-column stacked layout.

test_cases.scenario: A team created in Teams appears in team selection dropdowns in other modules
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a new team named 'QA Team' on the Teams page.
2. Navigate to another module that has a team assignment field (e.g. Users, Projects, or Resource Plans).
3. Open the team dropdown or selector.
test_cases.expected: 'QA Team' appears as an option in the team dropdown of other modules.

test_cases.scenario: A deactivated team is excluded from team selection dropdowns in other modules
test_cases.steps:
1. Deactivate a team named 'Old Team'.
2. Navigate to another module with a team selector.
3. Open the team dropdown.
test_cases.expected: 'Old Team' does not appear in the team selection dropdown. Only active teams are selectable.

test_cases.scenario: Team members listed on the team detail page match users assigned to that team
test_cases.steps:
1. Assign two users to a team via the relevant assignment flow.
2. Navigate to the team detail page.
3. Observe the Members table.
test_cases.expected: The two assigned users appear in the Members table with their Name, Email, Role, and Status correctly displayed.

test_cases.scenario: Team code remains stable as a reference identifier across modules
test_cases.steps:
1. Note the code for a team (e.g. 'TEAM-0005').
2. Edit the team's name.
3. Check references to that team in other modules.
test_cases.expected: The team code remains 'TEAM-0005' after a name change. References in other modules still resolve to the correct team.

test_cases.scenario: Deleting a team frees the team name for reuse
test_cases.steps:
1. Delete a team named 'Beta Team'.
2. Create a new team also named 'Beta Team'.
test_cases.expected: The new team named 'Beta Team' is created successfully. No conflict error appears referencing the deleted team.

test_cases.scenario: Audit log records team create, edit, activate, deactivate, and delete actions
test_cases.steps:
1. Perform create, edit, deactivate, activate, and delete operations on a team.
2. Open the audit log module (if available) and filter for the Teams module.
test_cases.expected: Each operation appears as a separate audit log entry with the actor, action type, team name, and timestamp recorded correctly.
